titulo: From found to used: WebMCP as preparation
lead: SEO gets your site found; the next step is getting it used by an agent in the browser. WebMCP proposes that the page offer tools with a name, a description, and parameters. It's a W3C community draft, with no stable browser: it's worth preparing a test page, not rebuilding the site or promising rankings.
objetivo: register a read-only tool with document.modelContext.registerTool() on a test page, as preparation.

aprende.t: What WebMCP is and what state it's in (specification of 10/16/2026)
The fields of a tool: name, description, schema, execute
Feature detection, cancellation, and the manual path
Where your site would gain a tool, and where it wouldn't

hero_alt: A receptionist tidies the front desk of a small hotel, with a bell and a tablet, ready to help guests.

nos.detalhe: The agent has to find the page before it can use it. Without crawling, an index, and content in the HTML, no tool helps.
Today, browser agents read screenshots, the DOM, and the accessibility tree, as Google's guidance (web.dev) says. WebMCP adds a direct path: tools that the page itself declares.

Per the specification of 10/16/2026, the API lives in document.modelContext, only in a secure context (HTTPS). registerTool takes the tool and, optionally, a signal: aborting the signal takes the tool offline. There is no separate function to remove it.

Access goes through the "tools" permissions policy (default: the page's own origin). A page that doesn't use WebMCP can turn it off with Permissions-Policy: tools=(). An action that changes something (buy, send, delete) asks for human confirmation and server-side validation.

W3C Draft Community Group Report: the document itself says it is not a W3C standard and is not on the standards track. There are reports of tests in Chrome and no stable release date; sources disagree. Preparation, not a ranking factor.

secoes.legenda: First be found; then, in time, be used.

texto: Start with something that only looks things up: opening hours, availability, list price, public order status. Nothing that buys, sends or deletes.
If your site has no useful journey for an agent, the right decision is to have no tool.

A specific, verb-based name (consultar_horarios). A description that says what it does, what it returns and its limit ("read-only; does not book"). Each parameter with a type and a description in the inputSchema.

passos.titulo: Detect, and fall back to manual
texto: Register only if the browser exposes the API ('modelContext' in document). If it doesn't, the page stays the same for the person, with the manual path visible.
Keep the AbortController: aborting removes the tool.

The specification changed: the API now lives at document.modelContext. The old INEMA WebMCP courses and many guides use the earlier name, on the navigator object, and a declarative form on forms that does not appear in the text of the October 16, 2026 specification (to be confirmed in the explainer).
To go deeper (security, schemas, agents), follow the WebMCP Program, keeping this name change in mind.

secoes.titulo: A read-only tool, ready to copy
secoes.sub: Test page served over HTTPS. Replace the hours with yours.

blocos.conteudo:
Opening hours

Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday, 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. Sunday, closed.

This browser does not offer tools to agents. The information above is just as valid.

grep -c "registerTool(" horarios.html
# 1
# published: agente-ready detects the tool in the static code
python3 agente-ready.py https://seusite.com/teste/horarios.html --saida saida/teste

abas.html:
agente-ready found on inema.club 1 registerTool() call on document.modelContext and the policy Permissions-Policy: tools=(self); the WebMCP block closed at 100. On the news and eventos sites, with no tool, the block stayed at 29.

This measures preparation. No AI promises to cite or rank you better because of it.

• registerTool(tool, options) rejects a repeated name, an empty name or description, and an invalid schema.
  • options.signal: aborting removes the tool.
  • annotations: readOnlyHint, untrustedContentHint, consequentialHint.
  • Permissions-Policy: tools=() turns the API off on the page and in its frames.

secoes.sub: Don't touch the main site: use a test page.

exercicios.texto: Adapt the template to a real lookup for your business, publish it on a test page over HTTPS and open it in a regular browser.
exercicios.pronto: the page opens with no console errors, shows the manual-path notice when the browser doesn't offer the API, and grep for registerTool( returns 1.

exercicios.texto: List 3 journeys on your site and decide for each one: read-only tool, action with human confirmation, or no tool. Write down the reason.
exercicios.pronto: a short text with 3 journeys, the decision and the reason for each, and which pages get Permissions-Policy: tools=().

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: According to the October 16, 2026 specification, where does the WebMCP API live?
perguntas.explica: document.modelContext, HTTPS only. Older courses use the previous name, on the navigator object.

perguntas.p: How do you take a registered tool offline?
opcoes: By aborting the AbortSignal passed in options.signal.
By reloading the site from the server.
perguntas.explica: The specification has no separate remove function: the signal is what removes it.

perguntas.p: Why start with a read-only tool?
opcoes: Because it's the only one allowed.
Because it changes nothing in the world: the risk of an agent getting it wrong is low. An action that changes something needs human confirmation and server-side validation.
perguntas.explica: Look first, act later, and with confirmation. readOnlyHint makes that explicit.

perguntas.p: A client wants WebMCP to "rank higher on Google." What do you say?
opcoes: That it ranks in one week.
That it's a W3C community draft with no stable browser: preparation for agents, not a ranking factor.
That it has been mandatory since 2026.
perguntas.explica: The document itself says it is not a W3C standard. Selling it as ranking is selling a promise.

itens.texto: First be found (SEO), then be used (tools).
document.modelContext.registerTool with name, description, schema and execute; signal to remove; HTTPS.
WebMCP is a W3C community draft (10/16/2026) with no stable browser: preparation, not ranking.
